result.keyword: What's the best project management tool for a startup?
result.markdown:
For most startups, **Linear is the best project management tool if you're building a tech product**, while **Notion is the best all-around choice for an early-stage startup that wants to manage projects, documentation, and company knowledge in one place.**

The right choice depends on your team's size, workflow, and whether you're managing software development, business operations, or both.

Here's how I'd compare the leading options.

## Best project management tools for startups

![Productivity Stack 2025: The Tools I Actually Use Daily | BlazeRift Project](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/4-TFr-ckQa-9bk8x5VN6sHjvab4UlZlJSmaxKNZqzorDbJHhW9DZ8v93iaVDfIkiOzoQ9x20fGWVh1jqG14cmFmuMUJrmAEpojnY6HPNQuTrQU9N60U1XJ7CBUVFqcXv7Vql7t3Kw83XWIte6ogtmJCGxWNK9WER_Kx53zTD3Ok1fUBOX0LQAPsxApxNVahh?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Linear**

(Best for tech startups)

- Excellent product roadmaps and sprint planning
- Fast, clean interface
- Great developer workflows and GitHub integration
- Less suited to general business operations

Best for: SaaS, AI, and software startups.

[Linear website](https://linear.app)

---

![Finastra Customer Story | ClickUp™](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/OXxUksa73j7hoTxbYQ6zo3pspX36GflPBLMsRWXjhfWZTJdFq6md_tXaxCCc_3Kjh0xQSrUSgXoCYi3d5TOe48r-mvzFwLplQbgf4lhsH3q_bsATt_hAcyva5qI1DtZG8OasgRxxldReZAIfURcJdNdt2Br8nPVvqn-lCO5aR2MxpFl9QAiCxibf4gzehOOb?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. ClickUp**

(Best all-in-one solution)

- Tasks, projects, documents, goals and dashboards
- Highly customizable
- Good automation capabilities
- Can become cluttered if overconfigured

Best for: Startups wanting one platform for the whole company.

[ClickUp website](https://clickup.com)

---

![Project Management Hub Template by Gridvio | Notion Marketplace](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/6e1oG6Y_aW5V5yDl222hE8Y8t-T__05L0OPLqrtY2b6KrmvS_M-QH4eaVLv4afPJUAGCFGr_eoifL-Irt3_HiUqUmKW08dRjhIxW2MfVWL_nPAWNaujkMp5zdq2VbJkW7b3h6jvrTVNAFmmVU9MPLCBztqWrhslDc_LeRhpbcV451et11onvlpgBLkBnIYcR?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Notion**

- Project tracking and company wiki
- Meeting notes, SOPs and documentation
- Flexible databases and templates
- Requires some setup to build a good workflow

Best for: Early-stage teams building company processes.

[Notion website](https://notion.so)

---

![New: Asana’s Milestones help you visualize project progress • Asana](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/045PY8MNTZCNbuEY_9zoc2ZmyVm82bEUQrACKq4DMJ2rZRzBOKtwnHDDeSB865DF__R-b4CGI6GEhHdu4YJMzkB1qcjJuCRLXmMhkxG9zfIfGx-0L1EgDFt_aMUwOdh5HR45ijTcFpeq8HRM8juB5v_Vffpp7OzTfiaEKInBCXkUCm5590f5v87DKC8sKsga?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Asana**

- Excellent task ownership and accountability
- Project timelines and dependencies
- Good cross-department coordination
- Can get expensive as the team grows

Best for: Marketing, sales, operations and cross-functional teams.

[Asana website](https://asana.com)

---

![Monday Vibe | Build Custom Apps with Vibe Coding & AI Prompts](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/dZbPOy2ExCYPWkRUN-y8aNBArPHAy5RJyF2Fv3kOH8r0onm7GzQMtNgFLnlF_orijMr1L_hlS3rZ5CmII7wcg1sC5QIg6R8JlCgddpaNU2x9UGq4FrFp6DOJXu4JvN0TyREqPyEMky1tg6L3RhInST4tHJiMa0BGxgH61Ibvrnb8NABR1soD10zbitKXa9pg?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. Monday.com**

- Very visual project dashboards
- Easy-to-understand workflows
- Useful reporting and automations
- More structure than a tiny team may need

Best for: Startups with growing operational complexity.

[Monday.com website](https://monday.com)

## My recommendation by startup stage

| Startup situation | My choice |
|--------|--------|
| 1–3 founders | Notion |
| 3–10 employees | ClickUp |
| SaaS / AI startup | Linear + Notion |
| 10–30 employees | ClickUp or Asana |
| 30+ employees | Asana or Monday.com |


## What I'd actually implement

For an early-stage startup, I'd keep things simple\:

1. **Projects\:** One central project dashboard.
2. **Tasks\:** Every task has an owner, deadline and priority.
3. **Weekly planning\:** Set three to five company priorities.
4. **Documentation\:** Keep processes, decisions and meeting notes in one place.
5. **Reporting\:** Track milestones, blockers and progress.

Don't overcomplicate things with enterprise-level project management before you need it.

I'll use those details to recommend one tool rather than give you another generic list.
